record.paper_title: A realist view of the electron: recent advances and unsolved problems
record.original_question: How can one construct a mathematical model of scattering processes based on photon interactions for extended electrons, in situations where reducing the problem to a one-body potential problem, as in standard scattering solutions, is not generally applicable?

evidence.quote:
It shall not be hidden, though, that a mathematical
model for scattering processes based on photon interac-
tions has yet to be developed: not an easy task, it seems,
since the reduction to a one body problem in a potential,
like in standard solutions, is not generally applicable.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Model an electron as a spatially extended object (rather than a point particle) carrying its charge and spin densities, and consider its interaction with the electromagnetic field via the exchange of photons. Develop a mathematically rigorous framework for scattering processes between such extended electrons (and between an extended electron and other charged matter) in which the interaction is mediated entirely by photon exchange, without assuming that the dynamics can be reduced to a one-body problem in an external potential. Specifically: define the state space and asymptotic in/out states for the extended electron coupled to the quantized electromagnetic field; formulate the scattering operator (S-matrix) for processes governed by photon-mediated interactions; and establish existence, unitarity, and computability of cross sections for elastic and inelastic scattering in this setting, in regimes where the standard reduction to a one-body Schrödinger or Dirac equation with a fixed potential is not available.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of constructing a fully rigorous scattering theory for extended (non-point) electrons interacting via photon exchange, without reduction to a one-body potential problem, has not been resolved. Standard QED scattering is formulated perturbatively for point electrons, and rigorous nonperturbative constructions of interacting QED scattering remain open. No source was found that presents a complete mathematical model of the kind described.

status_evidence.title: Quantum electrodynamics - rigorous results
status_evidence.snippet: A fully rigorous, non-perturbative construction of interacting QED in four dimensions remains an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous QED scattering theory without perturbative or one-body reductions is not established.
